title: Grab and Move doesn't work with Mouse without Borders secondary systems
author: DL-Ohio
summary: Grab and Move reacts to the physically attached host's input rather than Mouse Without Borders forwarded input, so remote-system windows do not move and host windows may move instead.

confidence.rationale: Input origin is strongly isolated, but the exact MWB injection transport and secure integration boundary require code tracing.

judgment.rationale: Multiple users reproduce on 0.99.1 and 0.100.2 with PowerToys installed on both systems. Touchpad input local to the secondary works, isolating the defect to forwarded input identity/state.
evidence: Grab and Move works with the secondary laptop touchpad but not with mouse/keyboard forwarded by Mouse Without Borders.
With Grab and Move enabled on the primary, the gesture can move or resize a primary-machine window even while the pointer is on the secondary.
A 0.100.2 confirmation says both mouse and keyboard must be host-native; mixed local/remote input also fails.
judgment.recommended_action: Trace how Mouse Without Borders injects/forwards button and modifier state and expose a supported local input signal to Grab and Move on the active machine.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The public report is already reproducible. Maintainer-side two-machine tracing should compare physical, MWB-forwarded, and mixed input and define a secure module-to-module handoff that does not broaden trust for arbitrary injected input.

proposed_fixes.title: Bridge Mouse Without Borders input state to Grab and Move
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Grab and Move observes physical/local mouse and keyboard state, while Mouse Without Borders forwards input through a path that does not satisfy those checks on the secondary and can leave the host gesture active.
plan: Instrument both modules to compare physical, forwarded, and mixed button/modifier events and identify the missing state on the active machine.
Add a narrow authenticated in-process/module signal from MWB to Grab and Move for the active remote gesture instead of accepting arbitrary injected input globally.
Cancel host-side Grab and Move activation when MWB is controlling another machine and add two-machine regression coverage.
verification: Using two machines, verify Grab and Move with local secondary touchpad, fully MWB-forwarded input, and mixed local/remote input.
Confirm only the window under the active machine's pointer moves and disabling Grab and Move on the host does not block the secondary.

confidence.rationale: Input origin is strongly isolated, but the exact MWB injection transport and secure integration boundary require code tracing.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move reacts to the physically attached host's input rather than Mouse Without Borders forwarded input, so remote-system windows do not move and host windows may move instead.
known_information: PowerToys is installed and Grab and Move configured on both machines.
Mouse Without Borders is configured for relative mouse movement in one detailed report.
No active linked fix or assignee appears.
inferences: Grab and Move likely consumes local low-level/raw input that MWB does not reproduce on the secondary, while the host still sees the physical gesture.
A direct dependency between modules may be safer than trying to treat all injected input as physical input.
issue_context.analysis: The public report is already reproducible. Maintainer-side two-machine tracing should compare physical, MWB-forwarded, and mixed input and define a secure module-to-module handoff that does not broaden trust for arbitrary injected input.

Used the local secondary touchpad success and host-window misactivation as the main input-origin discriminator.

reproduce.title: Compare local and forwarded Grab and Move gestures on two systems
reproduce.module: Grab and Move / Mouse Without Borders
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: Two Windows systems with current stable PowerToys
Grab and Move configured on both systems
setup: Place a movable window on each system.
Configure the same Grab and Move activation chord on both.
Record whether MWB uses relative mouse movement.
steps: Use the secondary machine's local touchpad/keyboard to move its window.
Use the primary's mouse/keyboard through MWB to repeat on the secondary.
Try one local and one forwarded input device.
Observe whether the host window moves and repeat with Grab and Move disabled only on the host.
reproduce.expected_result: The gesture should act on the window under the pointer on the active machine regardless of whether input is local or forwarded, without moving host windows.
